target.title: Make adaptive refresh agent-aware on fresh installs
target.body:
## Problem and changed premise

[#2029](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2029) found that the replay-only activity candidate did not improve global p95 menu staleness, so that evidence did not support a production or default change. Main now has the local Agent Sessions scanner from [#1968](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/1968), which provides a live, attributable transcript-activity signal without adding a second detector.

The target here is narrower: while local coding is active, an unconstrained Adaptive decision should not wait longer than the old 5-minute default. Global p95 remains unchanged.

## Implementation boundary

- On a fresh install with no prior-launch marker, existing config, or stored cadence, `refreshFrequency` resolves to Adaptive and is persisted immediately. Existing installations without a stored cadence, and unrecognized stored values, retain the legacy 5-minute fallback. Every valid stored Manual, fixed, or Adaptive choice remains unchanged.
- The upgrade boundary is captured before migrations. Existing config plus launch markers present since v0.4 cover normal upgrade paths. A completely untouched, configless v0.1-v0.3 install left no durable state that can be distinguished from a new install, so that historical cohort follows the fresh-install default.
- Recent local Codex or Claude activity caps only otherwise slower Adaptive decisions at 5 minutes. Low Power Mode and serious or critical thermal pressure still win with a 30-minute delay. Recent menu interaction can still select 2 minutes.
- A new activity observation may pull a pending timer forward. It cannot postpone an earlier tick or start a provider refresh by itself.
- Adaptive reuses the local Agent Sessions scanner every 30 seconds. Agent Sessions presentation, remote discovery, Tailscale, SSH, and remote focus remain behind the existing explicit setting.
- The scanner entry point is `@concurrent`, so synchronous `ps`/`lsof` and transcript parsing cannot inherit the caller's MainActor executor. Structured cancellation, priority, and task-local values are preserved.
- With Agent Sessions presentation off, the scan result is reduced to one in-memory `Date`; PID, CWD, project, transcript path, and session identity records are discarded.
- Each scan is bounded to 64 agent processes, 128 Codex rollout metadata records, and 64 Claude transcript candidates per project. Adaptive-only scanning pauses under power or thermal constraints.

This differs from [#2039](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2039): the Agent Sessions UI and all remote work remain off by default. Local `ps`/`lsof` and known transcript-metadata observation are intentionally active when Adaptive is the effective cadence.

## Proof

![agent-aware-adaptive-replay.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5c95fdc-c9f0-4d48-8d92-4dae696928ec)

Frozen trace: 1,780 JSONL records, SHA-256 `b1e4aa33180b7c177293eb9ed16b45e24e026d259600fba2b1b67b931b904f0b`.

| Policy | Simulated refreshes | Per observed 24h | Active coding over 5m | Menu p50 / p95 | Constraints |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agent-aware Adaptive | 696 | 143.88 | 0 / 145 | 139s / 1093s | pass |
| Menu-only Adaptive | 694 | 143.47 | 4 / 145 | 142s / 1093s | pass |
| Fixed 5m | 1383 | 285.90 | 0 / 99 | 150s / 281s | 157 violations |

Compared with menu-only Adaptive, the activity signal adds 2 simulated refreshes (`+0.29%`) and removes all 4 observed active-coding delays above 5 minutes. Compared with fixed 5 minutes, it schedules 49.7% fewer simulated refreshes. These are policy-clock results, not observed provider requests or an energy claim.

Activity fields cover 462 of 733 decision records (63%); 185 of those 462 samples are active (40%). The trace comes from one machine. It samples activity at reconstructed decision points and does not replay the new 30-second callback. Timer tests cover the callback and pull-forward behavior separately. p95 is still 1093 seconds.

Scanner cost was measured separately on exact head:

- Current local state, 1 attributable Codex session, 20 runs: `153.0 ms ± 14.4 ms` wall, `134.3 ms` user plus system CPU.
- Synthetic stress, 12 agent-like processes and 512 recent rollout entries, 20 runs: `231.4 ms ± 12.4 ms` wall, `209.3 ms` user plus system CPU.

Both measurements include CLI startup. At a continuous 30-second cadence, those CPU figures extrapolate to 6.5 and 10.1 CPU-minutes per day on this machine. Directory metadata enumeration still scales with known session directories; the code limits record parsing and process/transcript correlation.

## Validation

- `make check`
- 37 repair-focused tests on the current head: settings rollout, timer integration, Agent Sessions projection, and Codex rollout parsing
- `SettingsStoreRefreshDefaultTests` covers fresh-install persistence, both prior-launch markers, existing config, String and non-String invalid values, and all 7 valid cadence values across fresh and marked states
- Earlier branch validation covered 9 focused suites and 136 tests: policy core, replay baseline and CLI compatibility, app adapter, timer integration, Agent Sessions projection, settings fallback, Codex rollout limits, and Claude transcript limits
- `make test`: groups 1 through 9 passed, then group 10 failed with the same 8 `ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreCLIStorageOwnershipTests` issues. The exact suite fails identically on clean `origin/main` at `d57fb5d0`; it is unrelated to this diff.

The released `adaptive-activity` replay CLI spelling remains a deprecated alias for `adaptive`, while `adaptive-menu-only` names the historical baseline.
